deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying the profinite fundamental group π = π̂_{0,3} of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, which is free profinite on l_0 and l_1, with l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1. He considers its outer automorphisms that preserve the inertia (cusp) classes L_0, L_1, L_∞ ('loc') and commute with the S_3 symmetry group of {0,1,∞}. He calls this group Γ = Autext_loc(π̂_{0,3}, S_3). This is the target of the outer Galois action of Gal(Q̄/Q).

Representatives. An element u is represented by an automorphism normalizing L_0 with:
- u(l_0) = l_0^χ, where χ ∈ Ẑ^* is the cyclotomic-type character;
- u(l_1) = int(g)(l_1^χ) for some g ∈ π.

The representative, hence g, is ambiguous up to g ↦ l_0^α g l_1^{-α}, with α ∈ Ẑ.

The relations on g (from p. 9 and this page).
- Commuting with the involution σ_∞ (the swap of 0 and 1) gives a relation g l_1^q σ_∞(g) = l_0^r, with q, r ∈ Ẑ^*.
- This relation is invariant under the ambiguity above, so (q, r) depend only on u.
- For τ (complex conjugation), g = l_1 and (q, r) = (−1, 1).
- In the discrete (non-completed) case, the solutions with χ = p = ±1 are g = l_0^α l_1^β with α + β = 1, α, β ∈ Z. This recovers the identity and the τ-type element.

NB on symmetry. Replacing L_0 by L_1 (via the order-3 rotation ρ) replaces g by ρ(g) and leaves q, r unchanged.

Invariants on Γ. Besides the cyclotomic character χ: Γ → Ẑ^*, he obtains:
- a function β: Γ → Ẑ, defined on the next page by σ_∞(g^{-1}) = l_0^β g l_1^β;
- a function γ: Γ → π/Ẑ, the class of g modulo the twisted action φ(α)·g = l_0^α g l_1^{-α}.

Main claim. The map (γ, χ): Γ → π/Ẑ × Ẑ^* is injective, and β is determined by γ.

Margin. γ_0: E_0 → π is a 1-cocycle on Autext(π, L_0); this is the cocycle property of the 'f_σ' function.

Modern reading. Γ is essentially the group later called (profinite) GT_0, or Out^#(F̂_2): S_3-equivariant, inertia-preserving outer automorphisms of F̂_2, i.e. GT̂ without the pentagon. The injection u ↦ (χ(u), class of g) is the Drinfeld/Ihara parametrization λ ↦ λ, f ↦ f ∈ F̂_2.
- Drinfeld kills the ambiguity by requiring f ∈ F̂_2' (commutator subgroup). Grothendieck instead quotients by the Ẑ-action φ.
- The relation g l_1^q σ_∞(g) = l_0^r is a version of Drinfeld's 2-cycle relation f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1, before normalizing f into the derived subgroup.
- β plausibly plays the role of Drinfeld's m = (λ−1)/2 in the 3-cycle relation. For τ: χ = −1 gives β = −1 = (χ−1)/2.

Purpose. To describe the image of Gal(Q̄/Q) → Out(π̂_{0,3}) by explicit combinatorial invariants, as part of the 1981 'Longue Marche' program.
errors: The discrete-case statement 'g = l_0^α l_1^β (α+β=1)' versus 'q=-1, r=1 ... β=-1' is hard to reconcile with τ having g = l_1 (α=0, β=1) without knowing the exact normalization. This is likely a sign/convention slip or a transcription ambiguity, not a mathematical error.

Injectivity of (γ, χ) is asserted without proof here. It is correct: an outer automorphism fixing l_0 up to the power χ and l_1 up to the conjugate int(g)(l_1^χ) is determined, since l_0 and l_1 generate π. The assertion that β is determined by γ requires that σ_∞(g^{-1}) g^{-1}-type expressions fix β uniquely. This is plausible (the next page asserts uniqueness), since l_0^β g l_1^β determines β in the free profinite group.

ideas.what: Group Γ = Autext_loc(π̂_{0,3}, S_3) of inertia-preserving, S_3-equivariant outer automorphisms of the profinite free group on two generators
ideas.modern_name: GT̂_0 / Out^#(F̂_2) (GT without pentagon); Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for GT; Ihara (1991) and Lochak–Schneps / Nakamura (1990s) for the S_3-equivariant description
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions the Teichmüller tower and the automorphism group of π̂_{0,3}/π̂_{0,4}. The 1981 'Longue Marche' manuscripts treat related material.

ideas.what: Injective parametrization u ↦ (χ(u), class of g mod l_0^α g l_1^{-α}) of Γ into Ẑ^* × π/Ẑ
ideas.modern_name: (λ, f)-parametrization of GT̂ elements / Ihara's map G_Q → Ẑ^* × F̂_2'
ideas.where_published: Possibly in La Longue Marche (1981, circulated much later). Not in Esquisse explicitly.

ideas.what: Invariance of the 2-cycle-type relation g l_1^q σ_∞(g) = l_0^r under the ambiguity g ↦ l_0^α g l_1^{-α}; the extra invariant β: Γ → Ẑ
ideas.modern_name: Drinfeld's relations (I) f(x,y)f(y,x)=1 and (II) with m=(λ−1)/2

ideas.what: γ as a 1-cocycle on Autext(π, L_0) with values in π
ideas.modern_name: Ihara's cocycle condition f_{στ} = f_σ · σ(f_τ)

missed.claim: A 1981 explicit definition of the S_3-equivariant, inertia-preserving outer automorphism group of π̂_{0,3} (essentially GT̂_0), with a proof sketch of its injection into Ẑ^* × π/Ẑ. This predates Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara (1991). Grothendieck normalizes g by quotienting by the twisted Ẑ-action l_0^α g l_1^{-α} rather than by imposing f ∈ F̂_2'.
missed.quote: L'application (γ,χ) : Γ → π/Ẑ × Ẑ^* , u ↦ (γ(u), χ(u)) est injective
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority detail for the GT story. It is partially known that Grothendieck anticipated GT in 1981 (Longue Marche), but this explicit invariant pair and the extra invariant β (apparently Drinfeld's m = (λ−1)/2) document how far he went.

deep.surprise_reason: The page explicitly defines what is essentially GT̂_0 and its (λ, f)-type parametrization nine years before Drinfeld. It is a notable historical detail, but the specialist community broadly knows Grothendieck anticipated GT in his 1981 Longue Marche material, and the mathematics itself is now standard.
transcription_corrections: 'en plus des conditions [?] [?] sur χ' should likely read 'en plus du caractère cyclotomique χ'.
'{+deux[?]+} fonctions remarquables {+β+}' is probably 'deux fonctions remarquables β, γ' (β with values in Ẑ, γ with values in π/Ẑ). The phrase 'à valeurs dans Ẑ' is attached to β.
'groupe {+déf[?]+} Autext_loc' is probably 'groupe défini plus haut Autext_loc(π̂_{0,3}, S_3) = Γ'.
In the second line of the case display, 'les mêmes[?]' is uncertain; it may be 'les uniques' or a reference to τ.
Margin: probably 'NB γ_0 : E_0 → π est un 1-cocycle sur Autext(π, L_0) ... [comme] pour Γ_{0,2} ... cas spécial'. It is largely illegible.
